children: Stoke Space plans to develop a more powerful reusable rocket after raising $1 billion in a funding round led by Point72 Ventures and Spark Capital.
The Series E financing valued the U.S. launch startup at about $10 billion, Reuters reported, citing a person familiar with the matter. Stoke has raised $2.3 billion since its founding in 2020.

The company will use the proceeds to accelerate development of its Nova Pathfinder rocket, which is expected to debut in 2027. Some of the funding also will support Nova Block 2, a larger vehicle scheduled for its first flight in 2029.

For investors, the financing highlights growing demand for alternatives to SpaceX as satellite operators build and replenish constellations. Stoke’s $10 billion valuation reflects confidence in its reusable technology, though the company still faces considerable development, testing and execution risks before generating regular launch revenue.

Chief Executive Andy Lapsa said Pathfinder missions are booked for several years, though he did not disclose the number of launches. Stoke, based in Kent, Washington, also has begun preliminary discussions with potential Block 2 customers.

Block 2 will use 14 Zenith engines, twice the number planned for Pathfinder. The increased power will let operators deploy larger spacecraft or more satellites per launch, responding to changes in the size and volume of customer payloads, Lapsa said.

Stoke expects the fully reusable Block 2 to carry as much as 15 metric tons to low Earth orbit. An expendable configuration could lift about 23 metric tons, putting its capacity near that of SpaceX’s Falcon 9.

Pathfinder will remain available for dedicated missions and smaller satellite batches. Its reusable version is designed to carry 3 metric tons to low Earth orbit, while an expendable configuration could lift as much as 7 metric tons.
Stoke is among a small number of U.S. companies developing fully reusable orbital rockets. SpaceX
is pursuing full reusability with Starship, while Rocket Lab’s
forthcoming Neutron vehicle is designed to be mostly reusable.

title: Stoke Space raises $1B to develop bigger reusable rocket
